reasoning: In operator()(TagComputeOrientOrderAtomNeigh,...) the entire body is wrapped in 'if (mask[i] & groupbit) { ... d_ncount(ii) = ncount; ... }' with no else clause, and d_ncount / d_distsq / d_rlist / d_nearest are persistent views reused across chunks and across timesteps (only d_qnm is re-zeroed, via 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_qnm,{0.0,0.0});' at the top of each chunk). The three downstream kernels are NOT group-filtered: TagComputeOrientOrderAtomSelect3, ...BOOP1 and ...BOOP2 all run over the full [0,chunk_size) range and branch only on 'const int ncount = d_ncount(ii);'. So for an out-of-group atom whose slot ii held an in-group atom in a previous chunk/step, ncount is stale and >= nnn: select3() runs on stale d_distsq/d_rlist, and calc_boop1/calc_boop2 write a fabricated order parameter into d_qnarray(i,*). The CPU reference (src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp) does 'memset(&qnarray[0][0], 0, sizeof(double)*nmax*ncol);' before the loop and then computes only inside 'if (mask[i] & groupbit)', so out-of-group atoms are guaranteed 0.0. The KOKKOS port has no such memset either, so even the 'stale ncount small' case leaves last-step values in place rather than zeros.
fix: Two changes. (1) In the Neigh kernel add an else branch that clears the slot: 'else { d_ncount(ii) = 0; }' (or, cheaper, Kokkos::deep_copy(d_ncount,0) before each chunk's parallel_for). (2) Mirror the CPU memset by zeroing the output before the chunk loop: 'Kokkos::deep_copy(d_qnarray,0.0);' after d_qnarray is (re)bound in compute_peratom. With d_ncount(ii)==0 the Select3 kernel already takes the '(ncount == 0)' path and zeroes d_qnarray(i,*), and BOOP1/BOOP2 return early.

reasoning: KOKKOS calc_boop1(int, int ii, int ineigh) handles exactly one neighbour and starts 'const KK_FLOAT rmag = Kokkos::sqrt(r0*r0 + r1*r1 + r2*r2); if (rmag <= static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(MY_EPSILON)) { return; }' -- returning from that neighbour's invocation only; the TagComputeOrientOrderAtomBOOP1 policy runs one invocation per (atom, neighbour), so the remaining neighbours still atomic_add into d_qnm(ii,*,*) and BOOP2 then normalises by ncount and writes d_qnarray. The CPU ComputeOrientOrderAtom::calc_boop (src/compute_orientorder_atom.cpp) has the identical test inside its 'for (int ineigh = 0; ineigh < ncount; ineigh++)' loop but the 'return;' exits calc_boop altogether, so qn[] is never written for that atom and stays at the memset 0.0. Real divergence, but only reachable when a neighbour sits within 1e-15 of the central atom (a coincident/overlapping pair), which is pathological; and the CPU behaviour it diverges from is itself questionable (silently zeroing the whole atom).

Leaving the current per-neighbour skip is defensible, but then the CPU style should be changed to match so the two agree.

reasoning: The lines exist: 'int lo = d_table_const.lo(0); int hi = d_table_const.hi(0);' in temperature_lookup. But the description of the mechanism is wrong on two counts, and understates the real defect. (a) The local copies are NOT a 'second truncation' that breaks anything: d_table_const.lo/hi are ALREADY integer views -- src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.h declares 'struct TableDeviceConst { typename AT::t_int_1d lo,hi; ... }' (and TableDevice/TableHost likewise), with the original 'KK_FLOAT lo,hi;' left commented out just above. Copying an int view element into an int is lossless, and 't1 = MIN(t1,hi); if (t1==hi) delta = -delta;' still fires correctly -- just against the truncated bound. (b) The actual defect is the int views themselves. src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.h:46 declares 'double lo, hi;' in Table, and create_kokkos_tables() (fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:564-565) does 'h_table->lo[i] = tb->lo; h_table->hi[i] = tb->hi;' -- a silent double->int truncation of the table's temperature bounds, while invdelta is kept as KK_FLOAT. energy_lookup then computes 'itable = static_cast<int>((thetai - d_table_const.lo(ispecies)) * d_table_const.invdelta(ispecies));' against a lo that is off by up to 1.0 K from the tb->lo used to build invdelta, so every interpolation index is shifted; with a fractional tb->lo, thetai clamped to the (also truncated) hi gives itable > tablength-2, an out-of-bounds read of d_table_const.de (extent tablength-1). The CPU energy_lookup uses tb->lo/tb->hi as doubles throughout.
